name: coverage-meaning
description:
For each core phrase, the paragraph nearest it by meaning, and whether the text covers the phrase.

threshold: the similarity from 0 to 1 from which a paragraph covers a phrase.

The report has a row for each phrase, in its order and with its index: url and number (of the paragraph), the paragraph, similarity (4 places) and covered (yes or no); with clusters also cluster_covered. A phrase with no words, or a text with no paragraphs, gives an empty paragraph, no similarity and covered no.

Example: semkit read --text "купить диван" --text "кресло" coverage-meaning article.txt --threshold 0.5 write -
-> купить диван, , 1, Купить диван в Москве. Диван угловой, диван недорогой. Углы дивана и кресла., 0.7356, yes; кресло, , 1, Купить диван в Москве. Диван угловой, диван недорогой. Углы дивана и кресла., -0.2111, no

text: a text file (.txt), or a table of url and text, that is cut into paragraphs like `split-paragraphs` does; the table file is read like `read` does.
cluster: the column of the clusters of the phrases in the current table (as `cluster-meaning` gives it); every phrase also gets cluster_covered, yes when any phrase of its cluster is covered.
model: the encoder, pulled once with `semkit models pull NAME`: e5-small, bge-m3, potion, or hf:<id> of a model of the Hugging Face hub. Without --threshold the step takes the threshold of the model; a hub model has none.

The step takes the working column as the core and adds the columns url, number, paragraph, similarity and covered (and cluster_covered) right after it; the rows stay.
